Job Title: Project Manager

Location: RWJ - New Brunswick

Department Name: Planning Design Construction

Req #: 0000258291

Status: Salaried

Shift: Day

Pay Range: $130,000.00 - $185,750.00 per year

Pay Transparency

The above reflects the anticipated annual salary range for this position if hired to work in New Jersey.

The compensation offered to the candidate selected for the position will depend on several factors, including the candidate's educational background, skills and professional experience.

Step into a high-impact role where your expertise in planning, design, construction, and collaboration will help shape the environments where exceptional patient care happens. As a Project Manager on the RWJBarnabas Health Planning, Design & Construction team, you will lead capital projects from concept through completion, partnering with physicians, clinicians, facilities teams, contractors, architects, engineers, and other stakeholders to bring complex projects to life.

The Project Manager role may be the perfect fit for you if you thrive on turning ideas into action, enjoy managing complex projects, and take pride in delivering high-quality results within established budgets and timelines. If you are a strategic thinker, strong communicator, and confident leader who can bring diverse teams together to solve problems and move projects forward, this opportunity offers the challenge, impact, and purpose you are seeking.

As a Project Manager, a typical day might include the following:

Managing capital projects ranging from approximately ~$25K to ~$25M from planning and scope definition through construction and completion.
Developing and managing project budgets, schedules, logistics, and overall project expectations.
Providing project management support of RWJBH Construction and Project Delivery Team through assisting AVP of Construction & Delivery with responsibilities related to the delivery of projects and ad-hoc requests.
Partnering with physicians, clinicians, end users, Facilities Management, and leadership to understand project needs and establish appropriate scope and budget.
Engaging and coordinating architects, engineers, construction managers, developers, estimators, equipment planners, contractors, and other professional partners.
Developing Requests for Proposals (RFPs) and negotiating terms and conditions with professional service providers.
Monitoring project performance against contracts, budgets, schedules, and established quality standards.
Reviewing invoices, change orders, approval letters, and supporting documentation to ensure projects remain financially and operationally aligned.
Conducting regular site visits to monitor construction progress, quality, safety, and adherence to approved plans.
Coordinating construction logistics, equipment procurement, services, and other activities necessary to keep projects moving forward.
Leading regular project meetings, communicating progress to stakeholders, documenting concerns, and driving timely resolution of issues.
Ensuring required applications and permits are properly filed with applicable local, state, and federal authorities.
Coordinating utility relocations, shutdowns, inspections, testing, and other activities that require collaboration between RWJBH personnel, vendors, and outside professionals.
Ensuring projects comply with applicable healthcare construction codes, standards, regulations, and requirements.
Managing multiple projects simultaneously while balancing competing priorities, deadlines, budgets, and stakeholder expectations.

The Project Manager Role Might Be For You If

You enjoy bringing complex projects from concept to completion and seeing your work make a tangible impact.
You are a natural collaborator who can bring physicians, clinicians, facilities teams, contractors, and professional consultants together around a common goal.
You are comfortable managing significant budgets, firm deadlines, and multiple priorities simultaneously.
You can resolve conflict, build consensus, and keep projects moving when challenges arise.
You communicate clearly and confidently with executives, leadership, end users, vendors, contractors, and project teams.
You have strong organizational and information-management skills and can translate complex project information into clear recommendations and next steps.
You understand the importance of healthcare-specific construction standards, code compliance, safety, and operational continuity.
You take ownership of your projects and are committed to delivering quality results on time and within budget.
You lead with integrity and are proud to represent the RWJBarnabas Health mission, vision, and values.

To be considered for this opportunity, you must have a Bachelor's Degree in Architecture, Engineering, Construction Management, or equivalent combination of education and related experience. You must have at least 5 years of progressive project management experience in a hospital, medical center, or healthcare environment with demonstrated experience managing healthcare projects with knowledge of applicable building codes, regulatory requirements, and healthcare standards. SHR Consulting Group, LLC is a small business delivering enterprise IT, cybersecurity, and program management services to the Department of Defense and federal civilian agencies. We support mission-critical infrastructure at the Pentagon and across the National Capital Region, and we invest in our people through competitive compensation, professional certification support, and long-term career growth on stable, multi-year programs.

Position Summary

We are a rapidly growing organization seeking an experienced Project Manager
to oversee a large enterprise DoD IT environment supporting the DISA Joint Service Provider (JSP). The successful candidate will provide formal project management for areas of focus within Engineering to Operations, ensuring scope, schedule, and resources are managed to Government-approved requirements. 

Key Responsibilities

With the direction of the IT PMO Lead, oversee end-to-end project management activities and deliver project schedules for initiatives and transitions.

Provide weekly status updates on all initiatives and maintain accurate status on a SharePoint site and within the enterprise project management system (PROMIS or equivalent).

Track initiative tasks and subtasks in the enterprise ITSM ticket system (Remedy/Helix), and document level of effort, time, and resources involved.

Create or update documentation required to support each initiative, including future O&M plans and supporting RMF artifacts.

Coordinate Platform Service project tasks for early lifecycle backups, monitoring, and patching; provide design and transition feedback to the JSP Transition team within 5 business days.

Update internal SOPs, Work Instructions, and CMDB records to reflect the transitioned project.

Maintain situational awareness of project lifecycles and provide Platform Services feedback on project scope changes in weekly status updates.

Develop and present project briefs to JPH/JSP Leadership and provide PROMIS inputs within 48 hours of meetings with Division leadership.

Apply industry-standard project management practices in accordance with PMI / PMBOK and ITIL service transition principles.

Minimum Qualifications

Five (5) or more years of project management experience on DoD or federal IT services contracts, including managing concurrent initiatives or technology transitions.

Hands-on experience using enterprise project management and ITSM tools (e.g., MS Project, Smartsheet, Remedy, ServiceNow) and SharePoint to manage portfolios.

Experience leading cross-functional teams across computing, storage, virtualization, applications, cyber, and operations disciplines.

Strong written and verbal communication skills; ability to brief Government leadership and produce executive-level project documentation.

Working understanding of DoD Risk Management Framework (RMF), STIGs, and IAVM impacts on project schedules and acceptance.

Demonstrated ability to manage scope, schedule, cost, risk, and stakeholders for IT modernization projects in a complex enterprise environment.

Education

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Information Technology, Information Systems, Cybersecurity, or a closely related technical field; OR equivalent combination of education, training, AND at least five (5) recent years of documented relevant project management experience.  

Required Certifications

PMP certification required (or DAU Level III PM equivalent); ITIL Foundation certification strongly preferred.

Security Clearance

U.S. Citizenship and a minimum active Secret security clearance are required for this position. All personnel must be able to obtain and maintain the required clearance level and must possess a valid DoD Common Access Card (CAC). 

Work Environment

100% onsite at a government facility within the National Capital Region (NCR), primarily at the Pentagon, Crystal Gateway, Taylor Building, Mark Center, or other JSP-designated alternate site. Must be local to the DC Metro Area with reliable transportation.

Benefits

Competitive salary commensurate with experience and clearance level.

Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage.

401(k) with company contribution.

Paid time off and eleven federal holidays.

Certification reimbursement and training support.

Life and disability insurance.

SHR Consulting Group, LLC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or protected veteran status.

new_jobs.title: Compliance Audit Program Manager
new_jobs.description:
At BWX Technologies, Inc. (NYSE: BWXT), we are People Strong, Innovation Driven. A U.S.-based company, BWXT is a Fortune 1000 and Defense News Top 100 manufacturing and engineering innovator that provides safe and effective nuclear solutions for global security, clean energy, environmental restoration, nuclear medicine and space exploration. With more than 7,800 employees, BWXT has 14 major operating sites in the U.S., Canada and the U.K. We are the sole manufacturer of naval nuclear reactors for U.S. submarines and aircraft carriers. Our company supplies precision manufactured components, services and fuel for the commercial nuclear power industry across four continents. Our joint ventures provide environmental restoration and operations management at a dozen U.S. Department of Energy and NASA facilities. BWXT’s technology is driving advances in medical radioisotope production in North America and microreactors for various defense and space applications. For more information, visit www.bwxt.com . Follow us on LinkedIn , X , Facebook and Instagram .

Welcome to BWXT

We believe in empowering our employees and cultivating a dynamic workplace that fosters growth and collaboration. Whether you’re an experienced professional or just starting your career, you'll find opportunities to challenge yourself, learn from seasoned experts, and contribute to nuclear innovation. We require a diverse range of skills to support our work in the markets that drive our business and welcome candidates from all backgrounds and life stages who are passionate about making a difference.

Position Overview

The Compliance Audit Program Manager serves as a key liaison for ensuring government compliance and effective communication within our finance and audit teams. In this role, you will support process enhancements and maintain rigorous compliance with government accounting regulations. Your expertise in financial reporting and audit readiness, coupled with strong analytical and communication skills, will drive success in this collaborative, high-impact position.

Location:

Hybrid in Tysons Corner, VA

Your Day to Day as a Compliance Audit Program Manager:

Provide government compliance guidance and assistance to the finance and compliance teams within the organization.
Contribute to the preparation of a wide range of government cost and contracting documents, including incurred cost submissions (ICS), forward pricing rate proposals (FPRP), cost impact statements, provisional billing rates, and final rate agreements.
Perform monthly unallowable cost reviews for the corporate home office.
Support government audits by coordinating between audit teams and BWXT segments, managing audit requests, and ensuring timely collection and delivery of all required documentation.
Review and assess business practices in areas such as estimating, labor reporting, cost recording, cost allocation, and related processes to ensure they comply with all applicable government regulations and reporting requirements.
Contribute to updating and maintaining the corporate home office disclosure statement, and support segment compliance teams in updating segment disclosure statements to ensure they accurately reflect current accounting practices and meet all regulatory requirements.
Communicate with corporate and segment leadership and staff regarding new and updated government cost and contracting regulations, as well as changes to government accounting principles and practices.
Conduct readiness and compliance assessments for business systems covered under the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS).
Collaborate with cross-functional teams—including legal, contracts, procurement, and program management—to ensure compliance with government accounting regulations.

Required Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Accounting, Finance, or a related field.
At least 6 years' experience in government cost accounting, government contracting, and regulatory compliance and reporting.
In depth knowledge of government accounting regulations such as FAR, CAS, Defense Contract Audit Agency (DCAA) guidelines, and Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP).
Prior experience with ICS, FPRP, CAS Disclosure Statements, and rate agreements.
Demonstrated experience developing or enhancing business practices and processes to support compliance with government accounting regulations, including DFARS business system requirements.
Previous experience with financial reporting and audit preparation for government contracts.
Experience working in collaborative team environments, preferably working within a geographically disperse team setting.
Strong analytical and problem solving skills.
Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite, particularly Excel.
Demonstrable written, oral, and interpersonal communication skills.
Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail.
Must be a U.S. citizen.
Must be eligible to obtain and maintain a DOE security clearance.

What We Offer

Competitive salary and benefits package, including health, dental, and retirement plans.
Flexible work schedules and paid time off to promote a healthy work-life balance.
Professional development opportunities, including mentorship programs and sponsorship for continuing education.
An inclusive atmosphere that celebrates new perspectives and supports collaboration between different generations.
The chance to be part of a mission-driven organization making a positive impact on the future of energy.
Opportunities for continuous learning and training to grow throughout your career!

Pay: $79,000 - $119,000

The base salary range for this position in District of Columbia (US-DC) at the start of employment is expected to be between $79,000 and $119,000 per year. However, the base salary offered is based on local job market factors, and may vary further depending on factors specific to the selected job candidate, such as job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and other objective business considerations. Subject to these considerations, the total compensation package for this position may also include other elements, such as an annual cash incentive in addition to a full range of medical, retirement, and/or other benefits. Details of participation in these benefit plans will be provided at such time the selected job candidate receives an offer of employment. If hired, the selected job candidate will be employed 'at-will,’ unless employed at a location and in a position subject to a collective bargaining agreement. The company further reserves the right to modify base salary (as well as any other discretionary payment, compensation or benefit program) at any time, including for reasons related to individual performance, company or individual department/team performance, and other market factors.

As a federal government contractor, BWX Technologies, Inc. and any subsidiaries, affiliates and related entities (“BWXT” or the “Company”) complies with all federal, state, and local laws and customer requirements regarding health and safety protocols. As such, all BWXT new hires will be required to adhere to applicable Company health and safety requirements within the workplace as a condition of employment.

Your Journey at Crowe Starts Here:

At Crowe, you can build a meaningful and rewarding career. With real flexibility to balance work with life moments, you’re trusted to deliver results and make an impact. We embrace you for who you are, care for your well-being, and nurture your career. Everyone has equitable access to opportunities for career growth and leadership. Over our 80-year history, delivering excellent service through innovation has been a core part of our DNA across our audit, tax, and consulting groups. That’s why we continuously invest in innovative ideas, such as AI-enabled insights and technology-powered solutions, to enhance our services. Join us at Crowe and embark on a career where you can help shape the future of our industry.

Job Description:

What It Means To Be a Consultant At Crowe

Consulting is a dynamic business focused on solving problems for our clients and serving our core markets through innovative solutions. As technology and AI continue to reshape the consulting landscape, we are looking for individuals who are curious, adaptable, and eager to learn. At Crowe, consultants are expected to build both technical and transferable skills, think critically, and use technology to solve real business problems. In this role, you will continuously learn, collaborate across teams, and explore how tools, including emerging AI capabilities, can improve efficiency, insights, and client outcomes.

In management at Crowe, you play a pivotal role in leading teams, guiding project execution, and deepening client relationships. You are expected to contribute to account planning, identify opportunities to add value, and ensure high-quality delivery. As your responsibilities expand, you take on broader account ownership, balancing project leadership with growing involvement in client strategy and solution development.

Success in this role comes from a growth mindset, strong communication skills, advanced critical thinking, and the ability to navigate new challenges with confidence.

At Crowe, we bring deep industry specialization and functional expertise to help organizations manage cybersecurity risk, protect sensitive information, and strengthen operational and business resilience. We are seeking a Cybersecurity Manager
to join our growing team of professionals focused on both evaluating cybersecurity and resilience capabilities and supporting the maturity of programs across clients’ environments.

As a Manager, you will work directly with client stakeholders to understand cybersecurity and operational resilience needs; collaborate with engagement team members to plan and execute assessments and enable sustainable cybersecurity and resilience programs; and deliver actionable findings and recommendations that enhance security posture, regulatory compliance, and business continuity.

Business continuity and operational resilience
Infrastructure and application security controls

Join us at Crowe and embark on a career where you can help shape the future of our industry.

Job Description:

What It Means To Be a Consultant At Crowe

Consulting is a dynamic business focused on solving problems for our clients and serving our core markets through innovative solutions. As technology and AI continue to reshape the consulting landscape, we are looking for individuals who are curious, adaptable, and eager to learn. At Crowe, consultants are expected to build both technical and transferable skills, think critically, and use technology to solve real business problems. In this role, you will continuously learn, collaborate across teams, and explore how tools, including emerging AI capabilities, can improve efficiency, insights, and client outcomes.

In management at Crowe, you play a pivotal role in leading teams, guiding project execution, and deepening client relationships. You are expected to contribute to account planning, identify opportunities to add value, and ensure high-quality delivery. As your responsibilities expand, you take on broader account ownership, balancing project leadership with growing involvement in client strategy and solution development.

Success in this role comes from a growth mindset, strong communication skills, advanced critical thinking, and the ability to navigate new challenges with confidence.

About The Team

We invest in expertise. You’ll have the time, space, and support to go deep in your projects and build lasting technical and strategic mastery. You’ll work with developers, product stakeholders, and project managers as a trusted leader and domain expert.
We believe in continuous growth. Our team is committed to professional development and knowledge-sharing.
We protect balance. Our distributed team culture is grounded in trust and flexibility. We offer unlimited PTO, a flexible remote work policy, and a supportive environment that prioritizes sustainable, long-term performance.

About The Role

The Cyber AI Security Manager
sits at the intersection of AI engineering and cybersecurity. You will help clients securely adopt AI while also helping Crowe reinvent how cybersecurity services are delivered using AI. You will assess and secure GenAI, ML, and agentic systems, develop security patterns and controls for emerging AI architectures, and partner with cybersecurity teams to identify, prototype, and scale AI-enabled capabilities that improve the speed, quality, and effectiveness of our client solutions. The role includes the following requirements:

Collaborate closely with AI developers, DevOps engineers, and product teams to identify potential security vulnerabilities, implement best practices, and ensure compliance with regulatory standards.
Support security assessments, penetration testing, and vulnerability management for AI systems to proactively mitigate risks.
Act as the security expert in designing, developing, and deploying secure AI and machine learning applications, with a focus on safeguarding personally identifiable information (PII).
Stay ahead of emerging cybersecurity threats, privacy regulations, and compliance requirements to ensure that our AI solutions continuously meet and exceed market standards.
Document security protocols, conduct training sessions, and promote security awareness within the team and organization.
Engage with stakeholders across multiple disciplines to refine security policies and procedures specific to AI and ML products.
Identify opportunities to apply GenAI, agents, ML, and automation to improve cybersecurity services and client outcomes.
Prototype and productionize AI-enabled security capabilities—for example, accelerating security assessments, threat analysis, vulnerability prioritization, control testing, evidence analysis, or security operations.
Partner with cybersecurity practitioners to understand existing delivery processes and determine where AI can improve quality, speed, scalability, or insight.
Evaluate emerging AI security tooling and determine where commercial products versus custom AI solutions make sense.
Help establish reusable AI-enabled cybersecurity accelerators, patterns, and intellectual property that can be deployed across client engagements.

Minimum of 7 years' experience in cybersecurity, particularly focused on securing software and data-intensive products.
Proficiency with cybersecurity frameworks such as NIST, ISO 27001, or CIS Controls.
Familiarity with AI-specific regulatory environments and ethical considerations surrounding AI deployment.
Experience with AI related frameworks such as NIST AI RMF, OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications / GenAI Security Project, and MITRE ATLAS.
Hands-on experience designing, developing, or integrating AI/ML or Generative AI solutions, including experience with LLM APIs, AI agents/tool use, and modern AI application architectures.
Demonstrated ability to identify cybersecurity use cases for AI and translate them into prototypes, production solutions, or scalable service offerings.
Deep understanding of AI/ML systems architecture and the associated security considerations.
Excellent communication skills, with the ability to clearly articulate complex security topics to both technical and non-technical audiences.
Proven ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams including engineering, legal, compliance, and business stakeholders.
Would require readiness to travel domestically approximately 40% of the time to meet client needs.
Certifications such as CISSP, CEH, CompTIA Security+, or relevant Microsoft Azure security certifications.
Bachelor’s degree.

Preferred Skills

Strong experience in penetration testing, vulnerability assessments, and security incident response.
Hands-on experience with cloud security practices, especially within Microsoft Azure, including identity management, access controls, and secure networking configurations.
Proven expertise in GDPR compliance, SOC 2 audits, and handling of sensitive PII.
Experience with data anonymization techniques and privacy-preserving machine learning methodologies.
Understanding of DevSecOps principles and experience integrating security into CI/CD pipelines.
Previous experience within professional services or consulting environments, demonstrating client-facing capabilities and problem-solving skills.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, capable of navigating ambiguous scenarios and rapidly evolving threats.

At BWX Technologies, Inc. (NYSE: BWXT), we are People Strong, Innovation Driven. A U.S.-based company, BWXT is a Fortune 1000 and Defense News Top 100 manufacturing and engineering innovator that provides safe and effective nuclear solutions for global security, clean energy, environmental restoration, nuclear medicine and space exploration. With more than 7,800 employees, BWXT has 14 major operating sites in the U.S., Canada and the U.K. We are the sole manufacturer of naval nuclear reactors for U.S. submarines and aircraft carriers. Our company supplies precision manufactured components, services and fuel for the commercial nuclear power industry across four continents. Our joint ventures provide environmental restoration and operations management at a dozen U.S. Department of Energy and NASA facilities. BWXT’s technology is driving advances in medical radioisotope production in North America and microreactors for various defense and space applications. For more information, visit www.bwxt.com . Follow us on LinkedIn , X , Facebook and Instagram .

Welcome to BWXT

We believe in empowering our employees and cultivating a dynamic workplace that fosters growth and collaboration. Whether you’re an experienced professional or just starting your career, you'll find opportunities to challenge yourself, learn from seasoned experts, and contribute to nuclear innovation. We require a diverse range of skills to support our work in the markets that drive our business and welcome candidates from all backgrounds and life stages who are passionate about making a difference.

Position Overview

The Compliance Audit Program Manager serves as a key liaison for ensuring government compliance and effective communication within our finance and audit teams. In this role, you will support process enhancements and maintain rigorous compliance with government accounting regulations. About The Team

At OpenAI, our User Safety & Risk Operations (USRO) team helps protect our products and users from abuse, fraud, safety risks, and other forms of misuse. We operate at the front line of real-world safety and risk management, translating user and operational signals into timely decisions, effective interventions, and improvements to our systems.

Within USRO, Risk Incubation & Systems builds the analytics, automation, monitoring, quality mechanisms, and operating systems that help teams identify risk, make sound decisions, and scale safely.

Our work spans emerging-risk detection, operational measurement, workflow automation, quality systems, launch readiness, and decision-support tools. We partner closely with operational teams as well as Product, Engineering, Data Science, Product Policy, Safety, Legal, and Support to identify high-leverage opportunities and build practical systems that improve outcomes.

About The Role

We are hiring a Technical Operations Analyst to solve ambiguous, high-impact operational problems using data, technical tools, and strong judgment. You will work as an experienced individual contributor across USRO, moving from problem definition through analysis, workflow design, implementation, measurement, and handoff.

The scope is intentionally broad and may span emerging-risk detection, operational quality, automation, launch readiness, and other priority programs. You will be expected to move between different problem areas as organizational needs evolve.

This is a hands-on role. You should be comfortable querying and validating data, building dashboards and lightweight automations, using AI tools to accelerate work, and working directly with operators and technical partners to turn incomplete information into practical systems.

Your work may also include data and operational monitoring issues for major cloud deployment partnerships—for example, validating pipelines and safety signals, investigating anomalies or discrepancies, improving reporting and escalation mechanisms, and documenting data limitations so partner teams can act with confidence.

Location / work model: London, UK; hybrid, 3 days/week in-office.

Please note: This role may involve exposure to sensitive or concerning content. Strong discretion, judgment, and resilience are essential.

In This Role, You Will

Independently scope ambiguous operational problems and frontier & emerging risks, and turn them into clear analyses, workflows, tools, or decision systems.
Analyze large and complex datasets to identify patterns, data-quality gaps, operational blind spots, and source-of-truth issues.
Build and maintain dashboards, monitoring, alerts, recurring reporting, and workflow automations.
Develop systems for detecting and assessing emerging risks, including classifier, evaluation, labeling, and human-review feedback loops.
Support major cloud deployments and partnerships by validating data pipelines and safety signals, investigating anomalies, and improving operational monitoring, reporting, and escalation.
Design practical quality controls such as sampling plans, golden datasets, validation holdouts, thresholds, human review, and fallback paths.
Use AI and LLM-based tools to improve speed and scale while applying appropriate testing, quality assurance, and human oversight.
Translate technical and operational findings into clear recommendations, tradeoffs, decisions, and next steps for partner teams.
Partner across Operations, Product, Engineering, Data Science, Product Policy, Safety, Legal, and Support to define ownership, requirements, and durable handoffs.
Document system logic, limitations, operating procedures, and maintenance expectations so others can run and improve the work.

You Might Thrive in This Role If You

Have 5+ years of experience in technical operations, data analytics, trust and safety, risk operations, product operations, or a related field.
Are strong in SQL and comfortable working with unfamiliar datasets, schemas, joins, denominators, and data-quality issues.
Have built practical dashboards, tools, automations, or operating systems and owned them from initial scoping through adoption and maintenance.
Can use AI and LLM tools to accelerate real workflows while independently validating outputs and managing failure modes.
Understand how to measure technical or operational systems using concepts such as precision, recall, coverage, error analysis, quality assurance, and human review.
Exercise sound judgment in scaled operations, including queues, escalations, reviewer workflows, capacity, quality, and incident response.
Move quickly in ambiguous environments, make thoughtful tradeoffs, and create structure without waiting for perfect requirements.
Communicate complex findings clearly to technical, operational, and leadership audiences and drive work through cross-functional partners.

Nice to Have

Experience in trust and safety, fraud, scaled or adversarial abuse, integrity, emerging-risk detection, or other high-stakes operational domains.
Experience supporting cloud, enterprise, or privacy-preserving deployments with constrained data access or specialized monitoring requirements.
Experience with classifiers, evaluations, golden datasets, labeling programs, reviewer calibration, or model-quality measurement.
Experience with Python, notebooks, data-pipeline troubleshooting, or other lightweight technical development.
Experience designing quality systems or workflows that involve vendors, BPOs, or distributed operational teams.

Whether you're supporting a Fortune 500 client or a local business, developing cutting-edge technology, or providing clinical services you'll work alongside dedicated professionals who share your commitment to excellence and make a meaningful impact. Join us in fueling our mission to protect dreams and restore lives, while building your career in an environment that values collaboration, innovation, and personal growth.

Be part of a team that makes a real difference.

Job Description

The Senior Program Manager is responsible for leading highly complex, strategic, and enterprise-wide programs that drive significant business outcomes. This role operates with a high degree of autonomy and is accountable for aligning large-scale program execution with organizational objectives.

The Senior Program Manager oversees multiple interdependent programs or portfolios, influences senior stakeholders, and ensures alignment across Product, Engineering/IT, Operations, Client Services, Finance, and external partners. This role translates strategic priorities into executable roadmaps while driving accountability, governance, and measurable value delivery.

The Senior Program Manager serves as a trusted advisor to leadership and resolves ambiguous and high-impact challenges.

Program Leadership & Delivery:

Own end-to-end delivery of large-scale, enterprise-level programs or portfolios spanning multiple business units
Define and drive program strategy, objectives, success metrics, and value realization plans
Lead integration of multiple workstreams, ensuring alignment to business priorities and long-term outcomes
Translate complex, ambiguous business strategies into structured execution plans and roadmaps
Ensure delivery of programs meets or exceeds business outcomes, timelines, budget, and quality expectations
Anticipate and proactively address cross-program dependencies, risks, and constraints

Governance:

Establish and evolve program governance frameworks and standards
Lead executive-level governance forums, including steering committees and decision boards
Provide clear, data-driven program insights and executive reporting, including financials, risks, and outcomes
Drive decision-making by presenting trade-offs, scenarios, and strategic recommendations
Ensure robust documentation and traceability of key decisions, scope changes, and acceptance criteria

Execution:

Drive resolution of high-impact risks, issues, and cross-functional conflicts
Ensure readiness and alignment for major milestones, including testing, GTM and go-live
Lead continuous improvement initiatives to enhance delivery speed, predictability, and quality
Balance competing priorities while maintaining focus on strategic goals

Collaboration:

Partner with functional managers, senior leaders, executives, and key stakeholders to align on priorities and outcomes
Influence decision-making across organizational boundaries without direct authority
Lead and mentor program managers and project managers, driving consistency and capability growth
Build and maintain strong relationships across internal teams, clients, and external partners
Act as a key escalation point for critical issues and ensure timely resolution

Qualifications

Minimum Education:

Bachelor’s degree in business, Information Systems, Engineering, Finance, or a related field
PMP, PgMP, or equivalent certification preferred

Required Skills and Experience:

12+ years of experience leading complex, cross-functional programs or program portfolios
Proven experience delivering enterprise-scale initiatives with significant business impact
Demonstrated ability to operate with high independence and influence senior/executive stakeholders
Strong expertise in program governance and strategic planning
Advanced knowledge of Waterfall, Agile, and hybrid delivery methodologies
Exceptional leadership, communication, and stakeholder management skills

Desired Skills and Experience:

MBA or post‑graduate coursework
Experience in SaaS or technology-enabled services environments
Familiarity with tools such as Confluence, Wrike, Azure DevOps, MS Project, SharePoint, or Salesforce

Benefits

We’re committed to supporting your ultimate well-being through our total compensation package offerings that support your health, wealth and self. These offerings include Medical, Dental, Vision, Health Savings Accounts / Flexible Spending Accounts, Life and AD&D Insurance, 401(k), Tuition Reimbursement, and an array of resources that encourage a lifetime of healthier living. Benefits eligibility may differ depending on full-time or part-time status. Compensation depends on the applicable US geographic market. The expected base pay for this position ranges from $120,300 - $140,000 annually, and will be based on a number of additional factors including skills, experience, and education.

The Company is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, status as a protected veteran, among other things, or status as a qualified individual with disability.

new_jobs.title: Program Manager - EV Charging
new_jobs.description:
Join Our EV Charging Team!

Ecology Action is dedicated to creating a sustainable future by delivering innovative solutions that reduce emissions and improve efficiency. We are seeking a Southern California Based
Electric Vehicle Charging (EV-C) Program Manager
to help lead Ecology Action’s technical assistance programs that support multifamily and small business property owners to construct level 1, level 2 and Direct current (DC) fast EV chargers. 

About Ecology Action

At Ecology Action, we believe every person counts and every action matters. We've made it our mission to advance equitable community climate solutions and reduce GHG emissions through partnership, education and action. Every action we take today can create the future we want-one where people and planet can thrive together. Join Ecology Action in building a sustainable future where equity, resilience, and innovation are at the core. Together, we can make it happen.

About the Role

The EV-C Program Manager will directly manage consultants involved in EV planning and engineering, as well as contractors for work specific to the construction of EV chargers. They will be responsible for meeting performance deliverables for contract agreement implementation for Ecology Action’s EV Charging technical assistance programs, as well as program administration and performance, budgets and reporting for one or more technical assistance contracts.

What you'll be doing

Project Administration

Tracking, assessing and managing performance against contract budget.
Managing budget adjustments internally and with funders.
Providing progress reports to funders.
Reviewing and approving Ecology Action invoices to funders in coordination with the accounting team.
Processing and approving vendor invoices in coordination with the accounting team. 
Ensuring compliance with grant and contract agreement terms and conditions.
Participating in internal quarterly budgeting, forecasting, and adjustments.
Tracking and assessing performance against contract deliverables and lead on all funder contract requirements and data reporting.
Liaising with Central Services (IT, accounting, HR, Business Analytics) and Marketing Teams for project support.
Developing technical assistance workflows and processes for integration into Client CRM systems in collaboration with EV Program Operations team.
Preparing agreements and contracts with subcontractors, consultants, vendors, and program participants. Manage all contracts to scope and budget.
Ensuring that OSHA and Ecology Action safety protocols are followed during program implementation.
Maintain accurate and organized records of required documents.
Participating in team and staff meetings. 

Client Management and Stakeholder Engagement

Serving as the primary point of contact (POC) for clients (funders) and contract managers, ensuring strong relationships and alignment with client expectations.
Collaborating and coordinating with project partners to implement consensus-based approaches to program implementation.
Facilitating effective communication with stakeholders to achieve program goals and high-quality deliverables.
Building a Trade Ally Partnership program and coordinating with electrical contractors to bid on projects. The Trade Ally Program will provide program resources to electrical contractors' education on industry trends, best practices, and current technologies.
Generating recommended strategies for increasing program impact and functionality. Respond to challenges in program delivery.
Building and leverage relationships with key partners and government agencies to position EA to receive additional funding.
Designing and refining systems and processes to ensure program operational efficiency and scalability.
Leading on operationalizing new or expanded EV charging services as new funding sources are secured.

Project Implementation 

Conducting initial site walks with property operators to identify optimal parking spaces for EV charging stations near common electrical panels.
Communicating with property operators to identify and document electrical loads, site constraints, parking logistics and preferences for shared or assigned EV charging. 
Scheduling and participating in technical site assessments with community and facility managers and staff. 
Presenting EVSE software payment settlement options that meet multi-family property operators’ operational needs. 
Preparing site-specific scope of work and project design. 
Preparing construction estimates and evaluating bids from EV charging installation contractors. Evaluate projects for cost-effectiveness. 
Presenting technical reports, scopes of work, and construction estimates to property operators.
Supporting property operators to prepare contractor bid packages and notices to proceed to contract for EV charging station installations, and/or issuing purchase orders to subcontractors for Ecology Action’s direct installation projects.  
Managing Ecology Action’s direct installation subcontractors to scope and budget
Supporting property operators with construction project management and equipment commissioning.
Coordinating with contractors regarding equipment troubleshooting, maintenance and operations requests. 

Lead Generation and Customer Acquisition

Enhancing Ecology Action’s existing relationships within the market, specifically with decision makers, senior asset management executives, public agencies and community-based organizations in one or more specific regions of California.  
Directly engaging multifamily properties, small businesses, non-profit organizations and public agencies to submit EV charging project applications.
Working with EV Charging program management and business development teams to innovate, identify, and engage new external sales channels and partnerships.
Building and maintaining a pipeline of leads sufficient to achieve/exceed program objectives and equity goals.

Work closely with EA marketing team to develop customer acquisition campaigns and collateral.
Managing training, support and performance of community-based organizations and other channel partners with execution of marketing outreach campaigns. 
Creating and managing systems to track, measure and evaluate marketing campaign and partner performance.  Recommend and execute adjustments to approaches that maximize performance. 
Reporting on outcomes of lead generation activities for funder reports.

What We're Looking For

A minimum of 5 years’ related experience and a bachelor’s degree in business administration, Construction Management, Electrical Engineering, Environmental Studies; or an equivalent combination of education and experience may be qualifying.
A minimum of 2 years of experience developing and managing budgets or contracts.
Technical proficiency and experience in developing and managing teams to deliver EVSE installation programs, or other construction and electrical trade related retrofits in multi-family communities, and/or public and commercial properties.
Experience managing multiple contractors and construction projects with prevailing wage requirements.
Experience with project and program management fundamentals, ideally in the EVSE or clean energy sectors (work planning, scheduling, resourcing, budget management).
Experience with public agency and utility contract management and reporting.
Familiarity with CA electrical code, Cal-Green code, and permitting requirements for EV charging stations.
Experience managing client relationships and acting as a trusted advisor or Owner’s Representative.

Preferred Qualifications

Master of Business Administration (MBA) or Construction Management from an accredited institution of higher education
C-10 electrical contractors license or DIR certified electrician in the state of California.
Experience in the EV market transformation space, including accessing rebates for, and/or owning electric vehicles.
Experience living/working in low-income and under-resourced communities and/or low-income multifamily housing.
Familiarity or experience with public agencies and nonprofits working on sustainable transportation and transportation electrification policies and programs in California.
Experience with customer resource management tool systems deployment.
Experience working in a “start-up” environment
Training in Crucial Conversations, or related skills.
Interest and passion for transportation justice, including helping community members to access safe, healthy, reliable, and affordable transportation supporting access to jobs, education, culture, and recreation.

Work Environment

The physical demands described here represent those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.   
 While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to sit, stand, talk and hear, and use a computer keyboard and monitor.  
The environment is a mixture of an office setting and working out in the field. Most project sites will be located in Los Angeles and Ventura Counties, 
This position can be hybrid (home/office) or remote and may require the employee to occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds.  
Are You Ready?

Don't meet every single requirement? If you're excited about this role but your experience doesn't align perfectly with every qualification, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

Compensation: $105,000 - $130,000

new_jobs.description:
Compensation & Location

Location: Rosemead, CA

Schedule: Full-time, long-term contract

Work Type: Hybrid

Pay Range: $93.00 – $100.00 per hour (based on experience & internal equity)

Benefits:
Health, Dental, Vision, Life Insurance, 401k, Continuing & On-Demand Education

📍 Must be willing to work onsite in Rosemead, CA as required

‼️ W2 ONLY — No C2C, No 3rd Parties

Position Summary

We are seeking an experienced Senior IT Project Manager
to support a major Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI 2.0)
transformation program within a large electric utility environment. This role will lead all phases of the project lifecycle and System Integrator (SI) engagement, including pre-planning, planning, execution, monitoring, and closure.

The ideal candidate combines large-scale IT program management, AMI/smart grid experience, IT infrastructure knowledge, financial management, resource planning, solution blueprinting, and vendor management
. This is a hands-on leadership position requiring someone who can manage the overall program while personally executing critical PM deliverables and bridging business requirements with complex technical solutions.

Key Responsibilities

Lead project activities across the full lifecycle, including planning, execution, monitoring, implementation, and closure
.
Coordinate System Integrator activities across technical and business workstreams.
Facilitate IT business process mapping and requirements clarification
to align functional needs with technical delivery.
Prepare and manage financial reporting for AMI 2.0 releases, including expenditures, budgets, forecasts, and variance analysis
.
Develop comprehensive resource plans
based on technical scope, required roles, skill sets, effort, and cost estimates.
Coordinate resources across integration, data, infrastructure, and testing
workstreams.
Support development and refinement of the technical solution blueprint
, including scope, schedule, budget, infrastructure, data flows, and system interfaces.
Plan and coordinate the Planning & Analyze phases
, including solution-design validation and technical feasibility reviews.
Prepare technical teams for Build activities, including environment readiness, development sequencing, testing strategy, and deployment rollout
.
Coordinate cross-functional business and technical teams to maintain alignment with project milestones and deliverables.
Track project scope against baseline requirements and maintain requirements-to-design-to-delivery traceability
.
Manage the change-control process
, documenting changes and evaluating schedule, cost, resource, and technical impacts.
Identify project risks and opportunities and develop appropriate corrective actions.
Escalate significant risks, issues, dependencies, and scope changes to senior leadership.
Maintain project and financial documentation to support audit and compliance requirements
.
Support procurement activities, vendor management, and IT contract negotiations
.
Personally execute day-to-day project management deliverables while providing leadership and coordination across the broader program.

What This Person Will Be Working On

A major enterprise AMI 2.0 / Advanced Metering Infrastructure transformation program
.
Large-scale electric utility technology and infrastructure implementation.
AMI solution planning, technical blueprinting, and implementation readiness.
System Integrator coordination and technical delivery governance.
IT infrastructure, system integrations, interfaces, and data flows.
Resource and capacity planning across multiple technical workstreams.
Financial management, forecasting, and expenditure tracking.
Technical and business process alignment.
Solution-design validation and technical feasibility.
Testing strategy, environment readiness, and deployment planning.
Vendor, procurement, and contract-management activities.
Risk, issue, dependency, scope, and change management.

Required Skills & Experience

Bachelor’s degree
in Business Administration, Information Technology, or a related field.
3+ years of large-scale IT program/project management experience
within utilities or another regulated industry.
Experience with AMI (Advanced Metering Infrastructure), smart grid, or large electric utility technology/infrastructure programs
.
AMI 1.0 or AMI 2.0 experience strongly preferred
, with at least some AMI 1.0 exposure expected.
Experience managing large, complex IT programs
from planning through implementation.
Strong experience with resource planning, solution blueprinting, implementation planning, and end-to-end delivery management
.
Broad knowledge of IT infrastructure
with the ability to understand the complete technical landscape and identify delivery gaps.
Experience coordinating technical workstreams involving infrastructure, integrations, data, environments, and testing
.
Experience with project financial management, including budgets, expenditures, forecasts, and variance analysis
.
Strong risk, issue, dependency, scope, and change management
experience.
Ability to coordinate cross-functional business and technical teams.
Strong understanding of the relationship between business requirements and technical solutions
.
Excellent communication, leadership, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
Ability to quickly integrate into a large, fast-moving program and deliver with an appropriate level of direction.
Ability to personally execute detailed PM responsibilities rather than functioning solely as a high-level program leader.
Adaptable, receptive to feedback, and comfortable taking ownership of additional responsibilities as program needs evolve.

Desired Skills

Direct AMI 2.0 implementation experience
.
Previous AMI 1.0 implementation or deployment experience
.
Electric utility industry experience.
Smart grid technology experience.
Experience communicating complex technical information to non-technical and executive audiences
.
PMP certification
.
Familiarity with utility regulatory requirements.
Experience with financial compliance and audit requirements
within utility or IT organizations.
Strong experience with System Integrator management
.
Vendor management and supplier coordination experience.
Experience supporting IT procurement and contract negotiations
.
Strong experience managing large enterprise technology vendors and consulting partners.
Experience working across highly complex, cross-functional enterprise programs.
